doc.title: Willie J. Humphrey and Willie E. Humphrey Interview, 1959-03-15
doc.interviewee: Willie J. Humphrey and Willie E. Humphrey

title: Time check, introductions to Mr. Thompson and goodbyes
summary: They note the time, introduce Professor Manetta and Mr. Thompson, who played banjo, and wrap up.

story.theme_name: Thanks and goodbyes: closing the interview
story.community_name: Closing the interview: thanks, goodbyes and tape running out

blocks.x: Yeah, yeah, yeah. Anybody know what time it is? Steve. Steve Lewis. You know if you heard about Steve? The piano player, yeah. Yeah. Huh? Ten after four.
I got ten after four. Ten after four. It must be later than that. We didn't.
Oh, it has to be later than that, Fess. I don't know if I'm wondering why I'm watching.

It has to be later than that because we didn't get here until a little after three and we've been... Oh, yes, after four. We've been talking almost an hour and a half here. I enjoy it every bit too. So it must be five o'clock. We must run along. Oh. Let this tape run on through here for a minute and we'll get ready to go. Yeah, Willi remember.
Well, Willi was way behind me though, you know. Oh, yeah. Little Willi. Sure, little. I was a big Willi.
He's got ten years on you though. It's ten after five. This is my uncle. That's my aunt's husband.
How do you do? Good to know you. I'm Mr. Monetta, Professor Monetta, Mr. Thompson. All right, Mr. Thompson.
You met Mr. Russell. I believe he was able to do Mr. Thompson. Mr. Collins. How do you do? How do you do? Please meet Mr. Thompson.
Did you ever play any music Mr. Thompson? Quite a little. Banjo. Oh, banjo.
Or guitar. Yeah. Oh, my way we used to have a quartet.
Six boys. We used to sing on the fire. It sounds so good on the river. Mm-hm.
